text: Which of the following statements about the legal status of subliminal messaging can be inferred from the text?
options: The US Congress successfully passed legislation to prohibit subliminal messaging following the 1958 theater incident in New Jersey.
The National Association of Broadcasters' code is a legally binding federal law that carries the same weight as the statutes in the UK and Australia.
While specific regulatory bodies in the US have expressed opposition to subliminal messages, there is no enacted federal law specifically prohibiting their use.
The 1974 FCC opinion rendered all previous amendments by the National Association of Broadcasters null and void.

text: In the context of the final paragraph, how does the author characterize the collaboration between marketers and social scientists?
options: As a "cabal" that uses psychological insights to exploit human vulnerabilities and unconscious drives without the subject's consent or awareness.
As a transparent effort to help consumers make better decisions by addressing their insecurities and aggressive feelings.
As a failure of the "Brave New World" model, as social science has proven unable to alter thinking and behavior in a real-world setting.
As a purely academic exercise designed to determine how psychiatrists can better treat the "unconscious fears" of the general population.

text: Based on the third paragraph, which statement best reflects the author’s evaluation of "subliminal stimulation" as a modern threat?
options: It is a major concern because it is nearly impossible to detect and is currently subject to no federal oversight in the United States.
Its threat is largely overstated because its efficacy is contingent upon a person’s pre-existing internal motivations and states.
It is the most effective tool in the "Hidden Persuaders" arsenal for conditioning young children to become "good consumers."
It remains a primary focus of US legislation because research has proven it can create new desires in people who were previously unmotivated.

text: According to the first paragraph, how does the "influence" described by Vance Packard differ fundamentally from the "fictional tales" of control mentioned?
options: Packard’s influence is depicted as more easily resisted because it relies on psychiatry rather than conspicuous physical power.
The fictional forms of control are presented as "strange and exotic," whereas Packard describes methods that are widely understood by the American public.
Unlike the fictional leaders who used visible forms of control, the entities Packard describes utilize methods that are often entirely imperceptible to the target.
The influence in Packard’s work is limited to political leaders, whereas the fictional tales focus exclusively on corporate executives and social scientists.
